reviews.text: [quote]A review copy was provided by the developer.[/quote] [quote]Follow my Curator page, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/41363546-Fruit-N-Doggie-Reviews/]Fruit N Doggie Reviews,[/url] so you can be updated whenever I post a new review.[/quote] [h1]Overall Rating - Seriously Flawed ★★☆☆☆[/h1] [h1]First Impressions[/h1] I was completely oblivious to Creeper World IXE (CW), unaware there was another game from that series coming out. Then again, I haven't yet tried the third and fourth releases, so I'm a bit behind. Regardless, I received an email with a review key. When asked about the unusual title, it was explained to me that this wasn't considered the fifth release, but a side game. [h1]Gameplay[/h1] In the games I played, spamming energy-producing units was crucial, but in CW, your unit count is constrained by the level itself, as it'll dictate how many of each you're able to build and work with. I have mixed feelings on this matter, although I'll admit, not having to saturate each stage with countless factories is nice. However, despite this change, how you combat the creeper isn't much different, except for maybe a few new units. In addition, I don't love how the creeper is displayed, because you can't tell from its color alone how much has built up. You can hover your cursor over a pool of it to get some idea, but checking the graph to see the total amount on stage seems to be the most helpful. The vast majority of my time was spent in Story Mode. Tangent is more or less the equivalent of side quests from an RPG, as they're optional levels you can play if you want a break from the central plot. Colonies is where you can play other people's custom maps. Alternatively, you can go into the Map Gen system, which allows you to play stages that are randomly generated. Whether or not it'd be any fun seems like a matter of luck, especially since there aren't any toggles for what features are included or excluded. If you have an interest in designing your own stages, you can go into the Editor, making use of various limitations and creeper types to create a unique challenge. I'd imagine you have to clear your own stage before making it public, in order to verify it's not an impossible scenario. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3383100600 [h1]Controls[/h1] Because this is from a series of games I'm familiar with, I have no problems playing it with the mouse. There's a few shortcuts you can make use of if you know the right keys to press, but I was able to navigate just fine using the mouse exclusively. One annoyance is how the ships would keep flipping direction when I was setting them up in a new place; I wish they'd keep their orientation unless I manually toggled it. [h1]Story[/h1] I was trying to stay on top of the story, but after several missions, I lost track of what was going on. Seemingly the human forces were making numerous strides forward, but then some people also went off on their own expedition 10 years ago, with mixed results. Part of the issue reminds me of when the first Disney Star Wars movie came out, when five planets got wiped out by a wanna-be Death Star. Sure, that's an untold number of victims, but numbers don't matter. An audience needs a personal connection, which was lacking here, as nobody has any personality, “Nooo, not Peterson! He was so... present during all that plot stuff. Who else will respond to the protagonist summarizing the story?” https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3383102053 [h1]Visuals[/h1] While looking at the store page, it seemed like a large emphasis was placed on the pixelated graphics, since you'd dig through the terrain, and create particle effects as the grains slide down the slope. I'm not sure this was worthwhile, especially when playing the game at a faster speed. Trying to do so made it stall and lag. Over time, it would buff out, yet I don't think it should have any problems, with both stages and the game itself being on the small side. Having everything function as an immovable solid, instead of turning into particles, wouldn't really change anything meaningful, but probably would make a big improvement to the performance. [h1]Sound Design[/h1] One of the icons on the right side of the screen is for the music player. It turns out there's only four songs available, which are set to play in a random sequence. Unless you looked up an ideal approach for all the stages, you'd spend some time with trial and error, so I don't think this is an adequate amount of tunes for the entire campaign, let alone the optional content. Considering the range of scenarios and how many planets you visit, a larger variety of songs could better set the atmosphere as your emotions switch from horror and desperate struggles, to rage, or a swelling sense of hope. The songs aren't bad, yet I believe much more could have been done in this regard. Also, if you leave the audio balancing as is, the sound effects of battle are pretty loud. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3383101522 [h1]Pros[/h1] 🌟 You can access tutorial information at any time, but some are more detailed than others. The ghost ship needed to explain how to send out its unit, yet I don't know what the “use key” does outside of that situation. 🌟 The layout of the stage does determine how you direct your advance. However, with an emphasis on excavating the terrain, to some extent, you can dictate the size and shape of your approach. [h1]Cons[/h1] ❌ I find the reference point in the story strange to follow. In one sense, it revolves around a kid you saved 25 years ago, but he's just fast-forwarded into adulthood with no context, and you take his POV. There's nothing to anchor the plot, with many important events happening 10 years ago. ❌ Certain stages have very annoying conditions or level layouts, making it seem artificially difficult. Why wouldn't you always produce and bring along valuable components for disposing of creeper? ❌ Despite having limited units at your disposal, the gameplay feels very similar to the other entries. [h1]Tips[/h1] 🔍 Some stages can only be completed if you create anti-creeper. You'll want to lead with your armada of ships, but use shields to build a pool of anti-creeper so it'll pour into the creeper once you breach the wall. Also, create a narrow entry point to limit how much creeper can spill out. 🔍 Excavating the land is a good way to start stages. It can expand areas where the creeper spreads, uncover efficiency crystals, accumulate resources, and acquire buried energy. [h1]Final Thoughts[/h1] Since this game wasn't even on my radar, I had no strong feelings as I installed it, and for a while, I had mixed feelings about the gameplay. I saw both pros and cons, yet it was taking me a while to adapt to new territory. By the time I was more than halfway into the game, I'd have to keep restarting the stage, because my reliable strategies suddenly didn't work due to things like spinning gravity. I was so confused why a containable amount of creeper suddenly lurched towards my units despite not having much mass to it. Even though I beat the stage, after a while, I got fed up with aggravating set-ups requiring me to save scum to make progress. It won't surprise me if in a short while, someone uploads a path to victory for every stage, but I don't want to have to take such a restricted strategy in order to win. Let me have some wiggle room, allowing for more than one approach to succeed. CW got under my skin, so I wouldn't recommend it. Honestly disappointed as I love the CW games... The biggest disappointment is the lack of decision making. The limit on unit amount means you can basically get away with building a gunship or two, focus fully on economy, then build the rest of your stuff within the first few minutes of every level. One of my favorite things about other Creeper World games is fighting against the clock, trying to push out that initial creeper, while still needing to build up your economy to fight off that impending massive wave in the future. There's no real decisions to make in this one. Digging new area is like "capturing ground" in old creeper games, which could be really cool. But you can't do anything with this new area. No collectors to place, limited reactors. There's no sense of real progression or powering up in this one. The amount of mindless afk is also not fun. Probably around half of my 90 minute playtime was spent afking (again making no decisions) and just waiting for creeper to be killed. It felt like a slog. Other CW games mitigate this by letting you continually build more weapons and economy to speed it along and give you something else to do while waiting. This game has limited resources, so there's nothing to do but wait for your paltry few ships to chip away at the creeper. Maybe later missions change this a bit, but I'm not really enjoying the game enough to push through to get there.

For me mostly a downgrade to the previous installments. This is much more of a puzzle than an actual strategy game. In previous games, you could be proactive and creative with your approach, you were constantly pushing in multiple directions, trying to keep approaches covered and figuring out how to best deal with the creeper. In this, what units you have is fixed per map, and the ressources you have access to are frequently limited. So there is really only 1 solution the game wants you to implement, and then its just ages and ages of staring at the screen slowly waiting for enough push to happen and then moving all your ships up bit by bit. Its... really boring actually.

They really changed the formula on this one. Reminiscent of the second game, we're back to the side-scrolling perspective. But there's no mass in this game, only power. You are limited in how much you can build, different from every other Creeper World game. And for me, I don't like this. Every other creeper world game, you could win in most situations with enough time. This one is more a puzzle game, and you'll have to restart if you don't do the puzzle right. Yes, I did have to restart in the other games, but if I could hold onto an area, I could stubbornly hold out until I push enough to win, which took a while. But that's how I played. That's not how this one plays. There's just too many limits to artificially increase the difficulty for me. And it's too different from the rest of the games. I should have passed on this one.

As a long-term fan of this series: This feels like the weakest entry by far. The core concept just doesn't spark joy. It's like when C&C moved away from base building. Having a limited amount of units is... just not the way to go? That simply means there's no strategy. An entire dimension of all previous games is lost and missions feel either trivial or overwhelming and unbeatable. A recent patch restored free building, which means that the game is now *just* an underwhelming title by a beloved developer whose every single game I will continue to support.

Creeper World IXE is a mix of Particle Fleet Emergence and Creeper World 2, with a secret mode in the final level that is none of the previous games. The Dev team is always helpful in discord and on the forums and keeps their games going far past post-launch that shames AAA studios with larger staff. The game makeup consists of a set of allowable ship units that mimic Particle Fleet, with a limit on how many you can build of each. It then combines an static energy system in a series of puzzle maps to beat the villain aka creeper makers. It has some new or changed stuff from the previous games. They also added a new physics component in that the rocket explosion will cause a creeper shockwave. This can lead to some terrible mishaps that could result in a full map restart or simply a 'lose a bunch, remake, and push again' scenario. If you are a fan of Creeper World 3, the length of campaign will disappoint you, but the game itself continues with post launch player maps, editor, and random scenarios. The replayability is figuring out how people pulled off a 15 minute clear when it took you 3 hours.
Creeper World IXE is more of the same, which is good. The new gravity twist is good fun, and shakes it up enough to be new again. At this price, it's a steal. Love it.
Very different to the previous one. Honestly doesn't feel as tight, some of the ideas seem half-baked though it's still pretty fun. You should check out Creeper World 4 before this if you haven't.

This is a brilliant game. But I believe it's been hindered by a very poorly made demo. Demo is 3 missions. Mission 1 is fine, as it teaches the basics. On mission 2 I felt overwhelmed. Mission 3 was just an absolute launch into the deep end. I loved the idea of the game so I purchased it anyway, and now we get a gradual ramp up to actually get to grips with all the games mechanics! Now i'm hooked. Great game. Terrible demo.

Had a lot of fun playing it, more than expected after seeing the reviews. The final twist at the end was awesome. Great game. There are some issues ofcourse where the balancing should be checked. Some levels too easy, some a bit tedious. The unit limit was ok from my perspective. With every level you get more and more units available. Power production was suprisingly not a deeper tactical game element as it was in the previous games. It could have been left out and you wouldn't really notice. There is no "map painting" power nodes here. Big thumbs up for the soundtracks ingame. They are awesome. I recommend this game as I was addicted each minute playing it.
It's ok. I prefer the top down Creeper Worlds. Maps feel more like a puzzle, even the random ones - less freedom. Still, it's Creeper World and fun for a little while.

I genuinely cannot even beat the 3rd/4th level "Frozen" and I cannot even remotely fathom what I'm doing wrong. All of my ships are blasting away at the creeper and after >30 minutes of in-game time there has been little progress. But here's the kicker - I DID clear enough creeper to completely isolate the breeders and thrower, but for some reason the Nullifiers won't do anything, so the Creeper keeps building and building until I have to regroup my units. And then the IXE Core (the level objective) fell into the massive pit of Creeper I dug below the breeders, meaning it got completely submerged and it would've taken 300 years to dig it out again with pivoting ships back and forth. I've tried this level four times now and the result has been pretty much the same but I also don't see any other options as the game is quite restrictive. Creeper building up in the same place and then exploding outwards when freed is such a confusing mechanic that seems to punish you for making progress. Idk, I got into Creeper World with 4 and I was quite excited for this one, but it just doesn't make much sense to me.

In a vaccum this might have been a passably good game, but in the context of the creeper world series this one was a miss. I didnt find the gameplay enjoyable and it always felt more grindy than difficult. I hope the series continues as I have enjoyed every other entry.

The themes match, but the gameplay is much less the take and hold territory with wonderful parallels between the sides and much more something puzzle-y where the creeper isn't actively a threat you need to manage and more a series of tools you use to figure out the intended solution for the map. Creeper World IXE is, unfortunately, a misstep in a franchise that once defined its own genre. If Creeper World 3 was the pinnacle—offering strategic depth, emergent gameplay, and a perfect balance of chaos and control—then IXE feels like a regression, doubling down on the weakest aspects of the series rather than evolving its strengths. The biggest disappointment? The perspective. IXE returns to the side-view format of Creeper World 2, which was always the oddball of the series. The joy of Creeper World has always been managing fluid, organic threats on a large scale, not dealing with confined tunnels and awkward vertical combat. This shift makes the game feel constrained rather than expansive, a downgrade from the strategic freedom of Creeper World 3. Then there’s the linearity. IXE doesn’t just feel more restricted—it is more restricted. Levels seem to have a single correct solution, forcing you into rigid execution rather than rewarding creative strategies. Part of what made earlier titles great was the ability to tackle problems in multiple ways, experimenting with unit placement and energy management. IXE strips away that flexibility, turning missions into puzzles where alternative approaches are punished with failure. And let’s talk about the story—or rather, the continued lack of one. By this point, the franchise deserves something more cohesive than "The Creeper is here again, deal with it." The developer has seen enough success to justify hiring a real writer to expand the lore beyond the same vague, half-formed narrative we’ve seen before. IXE, more than anything, highlights that the franchise is running out of new ideas. If Creeper World 4 was the last major evolution, IXE is proof that simply repackaging the concept isn't enough anymore. At this point, revisiting Particle Fleet would have been a more interesting direction. To give credit where it’s due, the pixel art is fantastic. The visuals are crisp, and the game has a nostalgic charm. But at this point, it might be time for a Command & Conquer: Remastered-style update—let players swap between high-quality modern textures and classic pixel art. The series has always prioritized function over form, but a refresh wouldn’t hurt, especially if it brings in new players. Ultimately, Creeper World IXE isn’t a bad game—it’s just a disappointing one. It leans into the weakest aspects of the series, strips away the freedom that made previous entries great, and offers little in the way of fresh ideas. If you’re a die-hard fan, you might find something to enjoy. But if you were hoping for the next evolution of the series, you’re better off replaying Creeper World 3—because IXE isn’t it.

I was worried to buy due to the negative reviews and lack of updates. The dev is doing a terrible job communicating that he is implementing features based on player feedback every week. I would have bought 3 months sooner if he had published "News & Announcements" instead of simple updates (as we can't see all updates on the game page). You see, if you click on "See all updates," you'll see that all the problems people complained about in the reviews are already fixed, and the dev is relentlessly improving. Summary: people complained, he added new features (quickly). The game is great. By the way, I also played all the Creeper games. I started with Creeper 3, then bought 2, 1... 4... By far, this is still the game series that I love the most. So yeah, I am not a "new player that haven't played the old titles". I played all of them: campaign, custom maps, dailies, etc. Is it worth it? Definitely. No Creeper game had a "pattern". This is what makes it so amazing. Every new title only has one thing in common: The Creeper. Mechanics, strategy, graphics (we went from 3D to 2D), units... apart from some core elements, we are playing an entirely new game. Do you know the effort it takes to build something NEW every time? This is not Kingdom Rush 5 using the same everything as Kingdom Rush 4, 3, 2, and 1. Cheers to the dev, and my deepest apologies for not buying sooner. If you, player, are reading this review, please go buy the game. Want a new experience? Buy the other titles in the series as well. If you, Dev, are reading this review, please use the Steam Announcements feature a bit more. And thank you for all your hard work and your passion. You gave me so many challenging and fun moments. Thanks. P.S.: I will be giving away prizes I've accumulated over 4 years to any positive review within the next 30 days. This is because I’m sick of people writing reviews just to "conform" to what everybody else is doing. Publish yours, comment here, and I’ll send you a prize. Simple. Let's support the dev, he deserves it.

Super excited for the game in concept, but within the refund period I’d gone through 10 levels that were just slogging against heaped up creeper without any real strategy besides “do something slightly faster”. Felt like all of the magic of the series was drained to allow for a sand particle. It’s like Creeper World 2, but I can only build 2 of each turret limiting options. It’s like Particle Fleet but the map is so small and static I don’t feel like I’m taking over areas and building a logistic grid. Upgrades boiled down to a single multiplier instead of any strategy. Particle system exists but felt largely unused. I’m excited for what creeper world comes next, but this was unfortunately a deep disappointment for me in the series.

The demo showed an interesting new graphical style, and interesting new gameplay. However, the full game is... uninteresting. I'm giving up part-way through the (single-player) campaign because it's just more of the same, over and over, each level adding in one uninteresting new feature you have to worry about. The levels waver between easy and impossible for no obvious reason. I want the Creeper franchise to keep succeeding, but this isn't the right way.

I like the game but I dont love it. I've played every creeper world and this one is more of a slog than the others and its mostly due to fractional amounts of the antagonist - creeper. You may not think that fractional amounts would be a problem but it makes a huge difference. A spot with .2 creeper is damaging just as a spot with 300 on it. Positions are more easily compromised, the higher ground really matters and you find yourself spending a long time trying to move forward to then be pushed back by a curtain of ephemeral creeper. Because if your ship is damaged then it stops firing to focus on repair which then causes a cascading failure in your defence line pushing you back 15min of game time.
Life before death. Strength before weakness. Gameplay before graphics.

This game combines Creeper World 2 and Particle Fleet in a real good way. I like puzzling out the map to figure out how to effectively blow up, burry and flood the creeper into nothingness. The mixing of elements to create acid or tnt is fun. Style and music is great. If I had an issue it's that my five year old mid computer doesn't handle all the pixels moving around.

Has some elements that could have been interesting, if touched up and properly balanced. But combining the fleet element of Particle Fleet with the side View of CW 2, just really limited your options on what you're able to do mission to mission--it doesn't even give you options on what to do with the upgrade gems, removing any tactical aspect to them by just providing flat bonuses whenever you pick one up. I could get past most of that though, if the game actually played like it was supposed to--the game eats up a LOT of RAM with the pixel graphics for EVERYTHING in it, which causes frame rate to drop significantly sometimes even put on the lowest visual quality setting. The story, while never really award-winning for any previous game in the series, actively contradicts stories from those previous games which was something the others managed to avoid. And the help sections? The audio is basically useless, no matter what I try it is a garbled mess that skips constantly, I just have to pause it to read it. Your use of AI did NOT do you any favors in this game, and in fact degraded the overall quality. I enjoyed previous installments in the series because they actively gave us new and different ways each time to engage the levels, gave us strategic options if one way wasn't working, and generally kept to the same themes even with the 3D aspect of CW 4--in fact the 3D aspect of that one even improved on your strategic options. Here, this game is just a grind every level, with very limited options no matter what you do. Overall, 2/10. Sorry, devs, I give you one credit for trying new things, but overall this one is a stinker. I do not recommend this to new players. You'd have been better off just making another Particle Fleet game over this.
I really like the other games from the Creeper world series. But this one is disappointing. Would recommend if on sale for less than 10 bucks. Otherwise not really worth it.

The game is so much worse compared to the other Creeperworld games. Just like many games before (ahem Supreme Commander 2) they stray too far from the original reason why people play the game. Freedom and unit spam. The maps feel cramped, and most of the game is sometimes just fast forward until a section is clear of creeper. I would recommend it if it's on sale, but just be prepared for a different experience from the rest of the games.

ive played a *lot* of creeper world games, and this just aint it, like, at all, that tower defense aspect you know and love? slowly building out your defenses, fighting the waves back and taking out those cores? *gone*, like, *completely,* you still take out the cores, sure, but you have a set amount of ships, and the gameplay just isn't anything like what you would expect from the series, it feels more like one of the spin off titles like particle fleet than an actual creeper world. honestly, even on sale, I would suggest you skip this entry.

Is it a short game? Or do I just want more more more? Either way, I play through this story, set it aside for a while, and then come back and do it again. Fighting the creeper is the best kind of grinding, and IXE is a great continuation of the series.

It has a different flavor from previous CW games, kind of a mesh in some ways between those and the Particle Fleet spin-off (great game, btw). The flow mechanics of the ships and fluids makes for a different feel of gameplay that has taken a bit to grow on me. I've let the game sit for a bit, and am returning to it to give it another run. I think it stands well on its own, and is still a solid Creeperverse entry. There's a demo available (at least when I wrote this), so give it a shot and see what you think. Be patient to give it some time to express itself and let its mechanics show through, and I think you'll be pleasantly surprised. You can tell this was a labor of love and an experiment, and I think it's solidly proven itself.

Been playing creeper world since I was a kid. This one has the best story, BUT it's not creeper. The game deciding what ships you have and how you approach the issue is not the creeper core. I'll say if you want an interesting game, maybe. If you want creeper world? No.

This is a strategy game where you position your ships to fight the "creep" which is this ooze that is destroying worlds. Each mission you get a new unit/tool that will help you overcome a very specific problem, and by the end of the game you are supposed to combine them to win. The game is a bit frustrating when you know you will win, it will just take you a few minutes to do so. The units I didn't find interesting. You don't get a lot of unique combos or options, and most of the mission involve you just slowly building up your forces, and taking out the enemy in small engagements.

Lots of day-1 players and purists have said that this is nothing like Creeper World. I beg to differ. This has plenty of weapons from, I think, Creeper World 2, and is using a VERY similar map style except with some extra Noita pixel simulation, and overall is an expected step from CW4, from tower defense, more toward RTS. There is some of my own bias, though, because I'm a big sucker for space fleet battling games and there are SO PAINFULLY FEW OF THEM, and this was a nice change of pace from Starsector as far as scratching that itch. The fleet ship limit, as well, was good for forcing you to be, gasp, CREATIVE with ship placement and timing.
It's pretty fun. You'll enjoy this if you liked creeper world 2.

It's got the same theme as the rest of the Creeper World games, but doesn't really play anything like them, not even Creeper World 2 which has the same sort of side view of the game world. There's no real base building compared to any of the others, and the default mode means you can only build a small number of ships or other units. Unlike Particle Fleet the limited ship options actually feel really restrictive, and it feels kind of like the Free Build mode is essential for it to feel like there's actual gameplay instead of a level being an interactive cutscene. The text is also harder to read than the other games, and can look really odd at times depending on the game resolution or zoom level. It just feels unpolished.

It was okay. Its not like the other creeper world games where you fight on a flat surface with an ocean of creeper coming at you and stuff but its got some interesting aspects to it. However, I do wish the story had been a little better. More thought out, better plot, something that wasn't so easily predictable. That part was the disappointing one really. I suppose it was just to get the game out and try something new but still! There could have been some more story, and additional missions. Each star only had a single mission around it, I had hoped to find star systems with multiple missions to choose from but nah. I also found myself not using the chemistry stuff all that much. Finding it easier to just brute force instead of having to make a shielded pot to drop stuff into, suck it back up, drop more stuff into, suck it back up, get the right mixtures, etc. I'll probably just try and grab the last of the achievements though and possible return to the other creeper world games. I'm not so sure I liked this one enough to keep playing it for long. But yea, it was an okay game. Sorry I can't give a soaring recommendation here. :P The small story and lack of many missions relying on player created content just kinda, bleh. :P

Creeper World is always a favorite for me, and IXE very much deserve a recommend! That being said, I think I prefer CW3 and CW4 over IXE. This side-on view and very slimmed down version of terraforming feels like it detracts from the fluid dynamics that makes Creeper World interesting. I have played for 50 hours and feel very satisfied with my purchase, but next time I want to replay a CW game I will probably not choose IXE
